overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and it leans strongly Republican, with a partisan index of about R+17. Jerry Carl, the well-funded Republican, has raised over $1.1 million and benefits from more than half a million dollars in outside support, while Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $100,000. Prediction markets give the Democratic side only about a 2% chance of winning.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals and the money gap. The expected margin is roughly 17 points Republican, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of polling but not enough to change the likely outcome.
